bphs_sanskrit: rāmo'vatāraḥ sūryasya — Rama is the incarnation of Surya
avatar_quality_in_chart: Surya in the chart shows where the Rama-quality manifests: dharmic rectitude kingly bearing loyalty to truth and luminous heroic action. A strong Sun = the capacity to act rightly without deviation as Rama acted even when it cost him everything. A weak or afflicted Sun = Rama's dharma untapped or distorted — the heroic quality present but unactivated or misdirected. The Sun's house shows the area of life where the sadhaka is most called to perform Rama-dharma.
difficulty_as_mercy_interpretation: Surya's difficulties (opposition debilitation eclipse) are not punishments but the times when Rama's quality is being tested — as Rama was tested in the forest. The Sun's difficult periods are the forest-exile periods when dharmic commitment is forged. Difficulty from Surya = Rama's dharmic test being administered. The suffering is the qualification.
seva_natural_when_active: Mangal arati — greeting the deity at dawn as the solar form of Vishnu. Rama-nama japa at sunrise. Leading morning program with full solar energy. Dharmic action in the world — making clear righteous decisions. Surya Narayana vandana at dawn.
bhava_quality: Vira rasa — heroic unwavering action; the warrior-bhava of Arjuna-type devotion: doing the right thing for Krishna even when it is painful and costly. The Sun-devotee is in vira-bhava: acting without attachment to fruit in the manner of Arjuna under Krishna's instruction in BG 2-3.
vaishnava_practice_for_graha: Surya-vandana at dawn. Rama-nama japa (especially on Sundays and Ram Navami). Offer red flowers or Tulasi to Surya Narayana at sunrise. Read one chapter of Valmiki Ramayana on Sunday.
nakshatra_ruled: Kritika (shared with Moon for pada 1); Uttara Phalguni (padas 2-4); Uttara Ashadha (padas 1-4)
source_verse: BPHS 2.5: rāmo'vatāraḥ sūryasya candrasya yadunāyakaḥ / nṛsiṁho bhūmiputrasya buddhaḥ somasutasya ca — Dan Nelson translation (parashara.net); SB 9.10-11 (Rama avatar)

bphs_sanskrit: candrasya yadunāyakaḥ — Krishna (Yadunayaka — lord of the Yadus) is the incarnation of Chandra
avatar_quality_in_chart: Chandra in the chart shows where the Krishna-quality manifests most personally: the inner life mind receptivity emotional depth and the capacity for intimate love. The Moon's house and sign show where Krishna expresses most directly in the native's experience. A strong Moon = the capacity for deep devotional receptivity — the gopi-quality of total openness to Krishna. A weak Moon = the Krishna-quality present but blocked by mental turbulence or emotional contraction. The Moon is the most intimate avatar indicator — it is Krishna Himself showing where He most personally dwells in the chart.
difficulty_as_mercy_interpretation: Chandra's difficulties (waning Krishna paksha; affliction by malefics; debilitation in Scorpio) are not punishment but the viraha — the periods of separation and longing that deepen the devotee's love. The waning Moon is Radha's viraha expressed as cosmic rhythm. Difficulties from Chandra are the separation-periods that intensify the love that will be fulfilled at the next Purnima.
seva_natural_when_active: Quiet japa in moonlight. Smarana of Vrindavan moonlit pastimes. Attendance at Purnima programs. Receiving katha and kirtan rather than leading. Bathing of the deity (abhisheka). Reading SB 10 (the rasa-lila). Preparing milk sweets as prasad. Ashtakala-smarana (the eight-fold daily pastimes).
bhava_quality: Madhura rasa — the most intimate devotional bhava; the gopi-quality of complete surrender and longing for Krishna; the Purnima-devotee open to receiving Krishna's direct presence. On Krishna Paksha: viraha-bhava — the beautiful burning of loving separation.
vaishnava_practice_for_graha: Purnima fasting and feasting. Chant extra japa on full moon nights. Read SB 10.29-33 (rasa-lila) on Sharad Purnima. Offer white flowers and milk to the deity on Purnima. Keep Ekadashi (the 11th tithi — the Moon's own fast day).
source_verse: BPHS 2.5: rāmo'vatāraḥ sūryasya candrasya yadunāyakaḥ / nṛsiṁho bhūmiputrasya buddhaḥ somasutasya ca; SB 10 (Krishna-avatar); BG 15.13 (Krishna as Moon)

bphs_sanskrit: nṛsiṁho bhūmiputrasya — Narasimha is the incarnation of Bhumiputra (son of the Earth — Mars)
avatar_quality_in_chart: Mangala in the chart shows where the Narasimha-quality manifests: fierce protective energy the capacity for righteous anger in defense of devotees the fire that destroys adharma. A strong Mars = the Narasimha-quality fully available — the devotee who can stand firm against all opposition for Krishna's cause. An afflicted Mars = Narasimha's fire without direction — aggression without dharmic purpose. Mars's house shows where the native is most called to be fierce and unwavering in dharmic protection.
difficulty_as_mercy_interpretation: Mangala's difficulties (debilitation in Cancer; malefic aspects; Saturn-Mars conjunctions) are not punishment but the moments when Narasimha's fire is being tested against its most difficult circumstances — as Narasimha emerged from the most impossible situation (neither inside nor outside neither man nor beast neither day nor night). Difficulty from Mangala = the pillar being struck; the more impossible the situation the more Narasimha's emergence is called for.
seva_natural_when_active: Narasimha-kavaca recitation (especially on Tuesdays). Vigorous physical service. Protection of devotees and the dharma. Standing firm in Krishna's service against opposition. Intense kirtan in difficult situations. Ekadashi vigil as the Mars-devotee's discipline.
bhava_quality: Vira rasa — the heroic-protective bhava; the unwavering resolve of Prahlada under persecution; the Narasimha-devotee who cannot be broken by any threat; courage that comes from being held by the Lord rather than from material confidence.
vaishnava_practice_for_graha: Narasimha-kavaca recitation on Tuesdays. Offer red flowers to Narasimha. Do physical service with full vigor. Read SB 7.8-9 (Narasimha lila) on Tuesdays. Perform Narasimha puja if facing opposition or danger.
nakshatra_ruled: Mrigashira (shared with Rahu); Chitra (shared with Venus); Dhanishtha (shared with Saturn)
source_verse: BPHS 2.5: nṛsiṁho bhūmiputrasya buddhaḥ somasutasya ca; SB 7.8-9 (Narasimha avatar — emergence from the pillar)

bphs_sanskrit: buddhaḥ somasutasya ca — Buddha is the incarnation of Somasuta (son of Soma — Mercury)
avatar_quality_in_chart: Budha in the chart shows where the Buddha-avatar quality manifests: discriminative intelligence compassionate wisdom the capacity to see through illusion and the communication of precise liberating understanding. A strong Mercury = the Buddha-quality fully operational — the mind that cuts through delusion with compassion and precision. An afflicted Mercury = intelligence without discrimination — Mercury's discrimination-gift present but not yet purified by devotion. Budha's house shows where the native's most acute intelligence needs to be consecrated to Krishna's service.
difficulty_as_mercy_interpretation: Budha's difficulties (combustion by Sun; retrograde; malefic aspects) are the periods when the Buddha-avatar's teaching is most needed — when discrimination has become confused and clarity must be won through effort. Mercury's difficult periods are the periods of philosophical confusion that ultimately produce sharper discrimination. The Buddha appeared precisely when confusion about dharma was greatest — so Mercury's difficulties are the dharmic-confusion that calls for Buddha-quality wisdom.
seva_natural_when_active: Philosophical study and teaching on Wednesdays. Reading Bhagavatam with analytical attention. Precise theological discrimination. Skilled communication of Krishna consciousness. Translation and writing seva. Bhagavatam class — giving or attending with sharp attention.
bhava_quality: Shanta rasa (cool discriminative equanimity — Sukadeva's model) or Sakhya (the intellectual friendship of discussing philosophy with Krishna as in the Gita itself); the mind that is simultaneously sharp and surrendered.
vaishnava_practice_for_graha: Read BRS or Jiva Goswami's Sandarbhas on Wednesdays. Study Sanskrit or Vaishnava philosophy. Give or attend Bhagavatam class. Do one precise act of philosophical discrimination — write a verse or clarify one theological point. Offer green items to Vishnu on Wednesdays.
nakshatra_ruled: Ashlesha (shared with Moon for one pada); Jyeshtha (shared with Mercury's own nakshatras); Revati
source_verse: BPHS 2.5: nṛsiṁho bhūmiputrasya buddhaḥ somasutasya ca; SB 1.3.24 (Buddha avatar — teaches ahimsa); SB 2.7.37 (Buddha's mission)

bphs_sanskrit: vāmano vibudhejyasya — Vamana is the incarnation of Vibudhejya (teacher of the learned ones — Jupiter)
avatar_quality_in_chart: Brihaspati in the chart shows where the Vamana-quality manifests: the guru-energy that begins in apparent humility and expands to fill all available space with divine wisdom; generosity that operates through dharmic surrender; the capacity to receive and transmit the wisdom of the parampara. A strong Jupiter = Vamana's three-step expansion available — wisdom that covers the universe; guru-grace fully active. Jupiter's house shows where the native has the greatest capacity to receive and expand the guru's wisdom.
difficulty_as_mercy_interpretation: Brihaspati's difficulties (retrograde; debilitation in Capricorn; malefic aspects) are not punishment but the periods when the guru-principle is being tested through apparent diminishment — as Vamana appeared as a dwarf before His cosmic expansion. The contraction precedes the expansion. Jupiter's difficult periods are the periods of apparent smallness that presage the cosmic three-step. Bali Maharaja lost everything to Vamana and received more than he gave — Jupiter's difficulty is the Bali-period of surrendering everything.
seva_natural_when_active: Guru-puja on Thursdays. Attending Bhagavatam class as student (receiving the guru's wisdom). Teaching Bhagavatam class (transmitting the guru's wisdom). Generous giving — of prasad knowledge and time. Honoring the parampara. Reading BG with a commentary by a Vaishnava acharya.
bhava_quality: Sakhya with the guru (the wise senior friendship of wisdom-sharing) or Vatsalya as the guru who cares like a parent for disciples; the Brihaspati-devotee in Jupiter-active times: receiving wisdom and expanding it generously outward through teaching and giving.
vaishnava_practice_for_graha: Guru-puja on Thursdays (honoring the parampara). Offer yellow flowers and turmeric to Vishnu or the guru. Give Bhagavatam class or attend one. Read SB 8.18-22 (Vamana lila). Be explicitly generous — give prasad time or money to devotees.
nakshatra_ruled: Punarvasu (shared with Moon); Vishakha (shared with Venus); Purva Bhadrapada (shared with Saturn)
source_verse: BPHS 2.6: vāmano vibudhejyasya bhārgavo bhārgavasya ca; SB 8.18-22 (Vamana takes three steps to reclaim the three worlds from Bali Maharaja)

bphs_sanskrit: bhārgavo bhārgavasya ca — Bhargava (Parashurama) is the incarnation of Bhargava (Venus/Shukra — both are sons of Bhrigu)
avatar_quality_in_chart: Shukra in the chart shows where the Parashurama-quality manifests: the fierce tapas that produces extraordinary capacity; beauty earned through the most rigorous self-discipline; the devotional aesthetic faculty fully engaged; the Bhrigu-energy of intellectual and artistic excellence. A strong Venus = Parashurama's laser-focused intensity available for artistic or devotional excellence; the capacity to produce extraordinary beauty through fierce discipline. Venus's house shows where the native's most intense tapas and aesthetic gift needs to be consecrated to Krishna.
difficulty_as_mercy_interpretation: Shukra's difficulties (combustion in Asta; malefic aspects; debilitation) are not punishment but the Parashurama-periods when the intensity of tapas is greatest — when beauty must be won through the hardest effort. Parashurama's entire life was a series of extreme austerities and actions. Venus's difficult periods are the tapas-periods when the aesthetic-devotional capacity is being forged through fire.
seva_natural_when_active: Aesthetic seva on Fridays: arranging flowers for the deity with careful attention to beauty; dressing the deity beautifully; composing devotional poetry or music; preparing sweet prasad with love and care; listening to or playing beautiful music for Krishna. Vaishnava arts as seva.
bhava_quality: Madhura rasa expressed through beauty — Rukmini's refined longing that produced the most beautiful love-letter in the Bhagavatam; or the artistic Sakhya of Vishakha who composes devotional poetry for the Divine Couple; the Shukra-devotee expressing devotion through the finest aesthetic work.
vaishnava_practice_for_graha: Deity dressing and flower arranging on Fridays. Compose a devotional verse or prepare a sweet offering. Listen to classical Indian music or kirtan. Read Rukmini's love letter (SB 10.52-53). Offer white flowers and fragrance to the deity.
source_verse: BPHS 2.6: vāmano vibudhejyasya bhārgavo bhārgavasya ca; SB 9.15-16 (Parashurama lila — 21 times clearing the earth of corrupt kshatriyas)

bphs_sanskrit: kūrmo bhāskaraputrasya — Kurma (the tortoise) is the incarnation of Bhaskaraputra (son of the Sun — Saturn)
avatar_quality_in_chart: Shanaischara in the chart shows where the Kurma-quality manifests: patient inexorable weight-bearing endurance; the willingness to support the churning of the entire universe without complaint; the slow grinding quality that purifies through sustained pressure. Saturn's house shows where the native's most demanding long-term seva is located — where they are called to be the cosmic tortoise bearing the weight without acknowledgment. A well-placed Saturn = Kurma's patient strength fully operational. A difficult Saturn = the weight being applied before the capacity to bear it is fully developed.
difficulty_as_mercy_interpretation: Shanaischara's most difficult periods (Sade Sati — 7.5 years of Saturn transiting the natal Moon; Saturn returns; mahadasha) are not punishment but the times when the Kurma-quality is most being developed. The cosmic tortoise was not punished by being asked to support Mount Mandara — it was given the highest seva. Saturn's weight = the highest seva assignment. Sade Sati = Saturn entrusting the native with Kurma's sacred task of supporting the churning of the ocean of their life.
seva_natural_when_active: Long-term patient service on Saturdays — cleaning maintenance infrastructure; serving sick or elderly devotees; doing the unglamorous work no one else wants to do; regular steady practice without glamour; maintaining commitments through difficulty; early rising for brahma-muhurta japa through all seasons.
bhava_quality: Dasya rasa in its deepest and most patient form — not the exciting dasya of Hanuman but the slow grinding patient dasya of Kurma; the devotee who stays when others leave; who does the work that never gets acknowledged; the Saturn-bhava is the deepest possible dasya.
vaishnava_practice_for_graha: Do the work no one else wants to do on Saturdays. Clean the temple or ashram. Serve elderly or sick devotees. Maintain steady sadhana through difficult periods. Do not skip practices during Sade Sati — increase them. Offer sesame seeds and black flowers to Saturn as Kurma-Vishnu.
nakshatra_ruled: Pushya (shared with Mercury); Anuradha (shared with Mercury); Uttara Bhadrapada
source_verse: BPHS 2.6: kūrmo bhāskaraputrasya saiṁhikeyasya sūkaraḥ; SB 8.7 (Kurma supports Mount Mandara during Samudra Manthan — the cosmic churning)

bphs_sanskrit: saiṁhikeyasya sūkaraḥ — Sukara/Varaha (the boar) is the incarnation of Saimhikeya (child of Simhika — Rahu)
avatar_quality_in_chart: Rahu in the chart shows where the Varaha-quality manifests: the capacity to dive into the darkest most chaotic situations to rescue what is most sacred; the ability to work in territories considered unclean or taboo for the sake of liberation; the shadow-energy that when consecrated to Krishna becomes the most courageous rescuer. A strong Rahu = Varaha's diving quality — the willingness to go where others will not for the mission's sake. An afflicted Rahu = the chaos of the eclipse without direction; the shadow devouring without rescuing. Rahu's house shows where the native is most called to enter difficulty for Krishna's sake.
difficulty_as_mercy_interpretation: Rahu's most difficult periods (Rahu mahadasha 18 years; Rahu transits; eclipse seasons) are not punishment but the times when Varaha's quality is most needed — when the earth (Bhumi Devi — one's sacred purpose) has sunk into the cosmic darkness and must be rescued. The confusion of Rahu is the cosmic darkness before Varaha's emergence. Rahu's eclipse of the Sun or Moon = the moment when the cosmic boar is diving — temporarily darkening the light as it descends to rescue the earth.
seva_natural_when_active: During Rahu periods: deepen japa practice (especially protective mantras); decrease material engagement and increase spiritual intensity; offer to Varaha-Narasimha (the two most protective fierce avatars). On eclipse days: fast extend japa do not begin new projects. Enter the difficulty without fleeing — this is Varaha's instruction.
bhava_quality: Dasya in extremis — the dasya of entering the most chaotic situation for Krishna's mission; the fearless Varaha-bhava of diving into the cosmic darkness knowing that the rescue is the seva; the shadow-devotee who goes where the light does not penetrate.
vaishnava_practice_for_graha: Fast on eclipse days. Chant Varaha-mantra and Narasimha-kavaca during Rahu periods. Increase japa during Rahu mahadasha. Do not begin new ventures on eclipse days. Offer to Lord Varaha at local temple if available — or read SB 3.13 (Varaha lila) on days of Rahu prominence.
sign_ruled: No sign ruled (shadow planet — exalted in Taurus / Gemini by various schools)
source_verse: BPHS 2.6: kūrmo bhāskaraputrasya saiṁhikeyasya sūkaraḥ; SB 3.13 (Varaha dives into the rasatala to rescue Bhumi Devi from Hiranyaksha)

bphs_sanskrit: ketormīnāvatāraśca — Meena (Matsya — the fish) is the incarnation of Ketu
avatar_quality_in_chart: Ketu in the chart shows where the Matsya-quality manifests: the drive toward liberation and final release; the capacity to navigate the cosmic dissolution-waters; the comet-like movement against ordinary current; the ancient wisdom that must be rescued and preserved before it disappears. Ketu's house shows where the native's deepest liberation-potential is located — and where past-life saturation creates a combination of extraordinary depth and potential disinterest. A strong Ketu = Matsya's swimming quality — moving through the waters of dissolution toward the source; moksha-orientation combined with deep knowledge. An afflicted Ketu = spiritual bypassing — liberation-desire without the rescue-mission.
difficulty_as_mercy_interpretation: Ketu's most difficult periods (Ketu mahadasha 7 years; Ketu conjunctions; South Node transits) are not punishment but the periods when Matsya is swimming through the deepest waters of dissolution — when the Vedas (one's deepest commitments and knowledge) are at risk of being lost. The confusion and disorientation of Ketu periods = the moment before Manu receives the Vedas back from Matsya. Ketu's difficulties are the dissolution-moments that make the subsequent recovery of knowledge more precious.
seva_natural_when_active: Liberation-oriented practices during Ketu periods: reading SB 11-12 (liberation teaching); BG 18 (final surrender chapter); releasing attachments consciously; completing unfinished karma; deepening the guru-relationship for transmission of knowledge; ashtakala-smarana as preparation for liberation. Offer everything to Matsya-Vishnu and let go.
bhava_quality: Shanta rasa of the liberated soul resting in Vishnu — the complete surrender of BG 18.66: sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śaraṇaṁ vraja. The Ketu-bhava is the shanta of total surrender beyond all modes — the fish swimming in the cosmic ocean without resistance to the current.
vaishnava_practice_for_graha: Study BG Chapter 18 during Ketu periods. Release one attachment per week consciously. Read SB 8.24 (Matsya lila). Fast on Dvadashi (the 12th tithi — day after Ekadashi). Reduce material engagements and increase simple practice. Offer black sesame and tulasi to Ketu as Matsya-Vishnu.
nakshatra_ruled: Ashvini (shared with Mars); Magha (shared with Mars); Mula
sign_ruled: No sign ruled (shadow planet — exalted in Scorpio / Sagittarius by various schools)
source_verse: BPHS 2.7: ketormīnāvatāraśca ye cānye te'pi kheṭajāḥ; SB 8.24 (Matsya avatar — the great fish rescues the Vedas and Satyavrata Manu from the cosmic flood at the end of the age)
